run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:34:39Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by real 504 Gateway Timeout responses at the proxy (operation 'ingress', ~15.0s durations), which began in the 10-minute window ending 2026-11-18T01:34:39Z, exactly the alert start. The proxy was not itself sick: its egress spans to frontend carried error=true / http.status_code=0 after 15s, and frontend's own /api/cart spans hung for up to ~500s and returned HTTP 500 because the cart service could not reach its Redis backing store. Cart's own logs and spans give the exact error: 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' (FailedPrecondition 'Can't access cart storage'), first log line at 01:34:58, with cart's Redis client spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE) stopping at ~01:34-01:39. The dependency that failed is the valkey-cart pod: the otel-collector's redis receiver, configured with endpoint valkey-cart:6379, stopped obtaining new readings at 01:34:39 (redis_memory_used_bytes frozen at 1.6311264038085938 MiB, redis_cpu_time_seconds_total rate 0) while the collector itself kept exporting, and the only valkey-cart Service endpoint is that pod. The valkey-cart container kept running (restartCount 0) with no OOM, no memory/CPU saturation and no events, so why the Redis server stopped serving is not observable from the available telemetry (valkey logs returned no data, no change_history). No evidence found for valkey resource exhaustion, cart CPU starvation as the trigger, proxy failure, node failure, or the stuck terminating cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s pod; effective runtime flagd flags and Cilium network policies could not be read and remain open.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's request error rate deviated at 01:34:39: error spans on span_name 'ingress' rose from ~2-4 error spans per 10m to 53.68 (10m ending 01:34:39), 271.58 (01:36:39), peaked at 880 (01:42:39), while its total 'ingress' spans fell from ~6387 to ~554 per 10m over the same period.

frontend-proxy error spans are 'ingress' spans with status_tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and durations of 15000297-15001202 us (~15.0s); the paired 'router frontend egress' spans carry error=true and http.status_code=0 with the same ~15s duration, and the parent load-generator GET/POST spans in those traces also record http.status_code=504.

cart spans in the incident window fail with otel.status_description 'Status(StatusCode="FailedPrecondition", Detail="Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis ... ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected()")' on 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and '/AddItem', with durations up to 479682021 us, and frontend's '/api/cart' spans for the same traces return http.status_code=500.

cart container logs show repeated 'Wasn't able to connect to redis'; the earliest matching line in the 01:25:00-01:38:00 log slice is 2026-11-18T01:34:58.139444Z (no matching line earlier in that slice), and the pattern continues through 01:41:15.

Immediately before the failure, cart-to-Redis calls were healthy: HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE spans at 01:32:39-01:32:41 have durations of 114-34726 us with no error status, and cart requests completed with http.status_code 200.

cart's Redis client spans stopped: HGET fell from 1530.4 per 5m (window ending 01:33:39) to 833.3 (01:37:39), 107.8 (01:39:39) and 0 from 01:41:39, and cart server error spans appear from the window ending 01:37:39 (GetCart/AddItem STATUS_CODE_ERROR 7.26-31.11 per 5m).

cart's Deployment sets VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, and the valkey-cart Service resolves to exactly one endpoint address, 100.96.2.228, whose targetRef is pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr in node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae.
The otel-collector configuration defines a 'redis:' receiver with 'endpoint: valkey-cart:6379', so the redis_* series in this Prometheus are readings of the valkey-cart Redis instance.

Redis readings from valkey-cart:6379 stopped changing at 01:34:39: redis_memory_used_bytes held the identical value 1.6311264038085938 MiB from 01:34:39 through 01:41:39 after rising every minute before, its rate is 0 from 01:35:00 to 01:38:00, and redis_cpu_time_seconds_total rate drops to 0 from 01:34:39 (state user_main_thread 0.00120 before, 0 after).

The otel-collector pod itself kept running and exporting after 01:34:39 (rate(otelcol_process_cpu_seconds_total[2m]) is 0.0175-0.0424 through 01:44:00; span metrics continued), so the frozen redis_* readings are specific to the scrape of valkey-cart:6379, not a collector outage.

The valkey-cart container stayed up throughout: pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is phase Running, Ready=True, container 'valkey-cart' state running since 2026-11-18T01:01:36Z with restartCount 0 and lastState empty; neither the valkey-cart, cart nor frontend-proxy containers define readiness/liveness/startup probes.

valkey-cart was not resource-starved: its container limits are cpu 10m / memory 10Mi while observed container_memory_max_usage_bytes was 4.82-5.43 MiB, memory working set ~3.48-3.71 MiB, CPU ~0.0021-0.0037 cores and CFS throttle ratio 0.019-0.076 across 01:14-01:46.
All 21 otel-demo pods were Running with restartCount 0 at query time, and all five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False.

Other services' own error-span readings stayed at a stable background: accounting 0 and payment 0 error spans throughout, and ad, fraud-detection and recommendation stayed at ~1.04-1.08 error spans per 10m both before and after 01:34:39.

cart and checkout also show their own error spans: cart 22.5-84 per 10m from 01:36:39 and checkout 9.21-14.46 per 10m from 01:40:39, while frontend error spans rose from 0 to 260.37 per 10m at 01:42:39.
The flagd feature-flag ConfigMap demo.flagd.json has every flag, including cartFailure ('Fail cart service') and cart-unrelated flags, with defaultVariant 'off'.

The only non-data-recorders Kubernetes events in the window concern a different cart pod: Pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s with reason Killing (75) and Warning FailedKillPod (30, 'context deadline exceeded' killing container/sandbox), recorded around 01:37:28; no event names valkey-cart or frontend-proxy.

The failing dependency that produces the frontend-proxy 504 alert is the Redis server in pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr: it stopped answering clients at ~01:34:39 simultaneously for cart (same node) and for the otel-collector redis receiver (different node, pod 100.96.1.218), while its container remained running; cart's redis failures, frontend's hung /api/cart calls and the proxy's 15s 504s are its downstream consequences.

Because the valkey-cart container neither restarted nor hit its memory or CPU limits while both a co-located client and a client on another node lost access at the same minute, the Redis process inside the pod most plausibly became unresponsive/wedged (e.g. blocked in an internal operation) rather than being killed, throttled or network-isolated per client; the exact internal state cannot be confirmed because no valkey logs or process-level signals are available.

A runtime feature-flag flip (flagd flags are copied into a writable emptyDir 'config-rw' that flagd-ui can edit, so the ConfigMap need not reflect the effective values) cannot be excluded as a contributing trigger, although the visible ConfigMap shows cartFailure 'off' and the observed cart error is a real Redis connection failure rather than a flag-generated cart error.

An OOMKill or crash of the valkey-cart container is not supported: restartCount is 0, lastState is empty, peak memory usage was 5.43 MiB against a 10 Mi limit, and no valkey or OOM-related event exists in the window.

The proxy was not the origin of the failures: frontend-proxy's CFS throttle ratio stayed at 0.0012-0.047 (dropping to ~0.001 after 01:40) and its error spans are 504s that follow a 15s timeout of its egress call to frontend, while frontend itself was blocked on cart.

Rejected: cart CPU starvation caused the Redis connection failures. cart's throttle ratio only rose after the first redis error (01:34:58) — from 0.18-0.23 to 0.83-0.90 of periods — while its usage (0.0095 rising to 0.0258 cores) stayed below its 45m limit, and a cart-side CPU problem cannot explain the simultaneous loss of the otel-collector's redis scrape from a different node.

Rejected: the stuck terminating pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s caused the errors. It is not in the cart Service endpoints (only cart-755465879b-t9mf7 is), so it received no service traffic, and its Killing/FailedKillPod events (~01:37:28) postdate the first proxy errors at 01:34:39 and first cart redis error at 01:34:58.

Rejected: a node-level failure of i-0146cb0d0caf26bae (hosting cart, valkey-cart, frontend-proxy, checkout, product-catalog, quote, postgresql) explains the outage. The node is Ready with no pressure conditions, and pods on it kept serving — e.g. checkout got gRPC answer codes back from cart and returned its own cart-derived failures rather than timeouts.

Inspect the valkey-cart container directly (redis-cli PING, thread/stack state of the valkey process, LISTEN state on 6379) and capture its stdout/stderr, since log retrieval returned no data for that container and this is the missing step to explain why the server stopped serving at 01:34:39.

Read the Cilium CiliumNetworkPolicy/CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy objects for otel-demo pod selectors, since Cilium CRDs exist in this cluster and these kinds could not be read with the available resource list.

Review the writable flagd copy (emptyDir 'config-rw' used with the flagd-ui container) or flagd-ui change history to confirm the effective flag values at 01:34:39, and consider raising the valkey-cart limits (cpu 10m / memory 10Mi) as a hardening measure, though neither is shown to have caused this outage.

gaps: No valkey/Redis application logs were returned for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr (fetch_pod_logs status no_data for the whole authorized window, container running since 01:01:36), so the reason the Redis server stopped serving cannot be established.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and unfiltered, so the alert expression and its exact threshold are unknown.

Effective runtime flagd feature-flag values are unknown: flagd mounts a writable emptyDir ('config-rw') used by the flagd-ui container, and flagd pod logs returned no data, so a runtime flag change cannot be confirmed or excluded even though the flagd-config ConfigMap shows every flag 'off'.

The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change, config edit or deployment update around 01:34:39 can be observed; no object in the evidence is seen applying a change to valkey-cart.

CiliumNetworkPolicy/CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy objects exist as CRDs but are not readable kinds here; a networking.k8s.io NetworkPolicies query for otel-demo returned an empty result (that query matched nothing, it does not prove no policy exists), so a network-level block between cart and valkey-cart is neither confirmed nor excluded.

kube-state-metrics series (kube_pod_*, kube_deployment_*) returned no metric names in this Prometheus, so pod restart/termination reasons could only be checked via the Kubernetes API state and events, not as metric history.

Error-rate series for currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote and shipping were not returned under the STATUS_CODE_ERROR selector, so those services are unknown rather than verified healthy.

The earlier cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s is absent from the Kubernetes pod list yet still has cAdvisor series (constant 27.79 MiB working set, ~0.0065 cores) up to 01:46:39 on node i-00702f4ac4662cf00; why it lingers in cAdvisor after removal could not be explained.
next_steps: Run an in-pod diagnostic on valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr (redis-cli PING/INFO, process stack, socket listen state) and collect its stdout/stderr.
Diff the effective flagd configuration and any flagd-ui edits against flagd-config for the period around 01:34:39.
Review Cilium network policies and host-level conntrack/socket telemetry for the cart and valkey-cart pods on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae.
